name: OSIRIS-APEX
intro: As OSIRIS-REx, this spacecraft grabbed rubble from asteroid Bennu in 2020 and dropped it off at Earth in 2023. It was not abandoned: it was renamed OSIRIS-APEX and sent to meet asteroid Apophis in 2029.
status: Active, on its way to Apophis (2029)
whyLeft: It has not been left. After its sample capsule landed, the spacecraft still worked, so NASA gave it a new job instead of switching it off.
repurpose: This is a salvage success: a spacecraft that finished its first mission was given a second one, to study Apophis right after it passes close to Earth in April 2029.

hotspots.title: The sample arm
hotspots.text: On 20 October 2020 this arm touched Bennu for a few seconds and puffed nitrogen gas to stir up rubble. The ground was so loose that the arm sank in about half a meter.

video.caption: OSIRIS-REx touching asteroid Bennu on 20 October 2020, filmed by its own camera. Real footage, no sound.

hotspots.title: The empty capsule spot
hotspots.text: The sample capsule rode here. On 24 September 2023 it parachuted into the Utah desert with 121.6 grams of Bennu, NASA’s first asteroid sample.

photo.alt: A cone-shaped capsule lying on desert ground.
photo.caption: The OSIRIS-REx sample capsule just after landing in the Utah desert on 24 September 2023.
photo.licenseEvidence: Commons page licence: “Public domain” (PD NASA); original source: This image or video was catalogued by NASA Headquarters of the United States National Aero.

hotspots.title: Overstuffed
hotspots.text: The sampler head grabbed so much that rocks jammed its flap open and some bits floated away. The team quickly packed it into the capsule, saving most of the sample.

hotspots.title: The dish
hotspots.text: This dish sends messages to Earth. It will carry home OSIRIS-APEX’s pictures of Apophis.

hotspots.title: Solar panels
hotspots.text: Two solar panels power the spacecraft as it loops around the Sun toward its meeting with Apophis in 2029.

funFact: Asteroid Apophis will pass so close to Earth on 13 April 2029 that people will see it without a telescope.
